ITEM.PTXT: A transmission control computer integrated with the engine control computer has been adopted. Various signals are communicated between the engine and transmission control computers to perform integrated engine control, achieving both smooth shift characteristics and excellent shift response at a high level.

Acceleration control (linear feel improvement control), NAVI AI-SHIFT and uphill/downhill shift control have been adopted to achieve smooth shift characteristics and excellent shift response, and neutral control has been adopted to improve fuel economy while the vehicle is stopped.
Diagnosis and fail-safe functions are provided for serviceability in the event of a system malfunction.

ITEM.PTXT: By integrating the control of CVT speed and engine torque, fine control is performed so that the engine operates on its optimum fuel economy line.

ENTRY.PTXT: The target engine output is determined from the target driving force requested by the driver, based on the accelerator opening and wheel speed.
The target primary pulley speed is determined so that the target engine output can be achieved on the engine's optimum fuel economy line, and shift control is performed.
The target engine torque is determined from the target engine output and the primary pulley speed, and throttle opening control is performed.

ITEM.PTXT: The driver's acceleration request is determined from changes in vehicle speed and accelerator opening, and control shifts to driving force control that provides a good acceleration feel. In this case, the acceleration generated for a constant accelerator opening is kept constant, and the engine speed increases as the vehicle speed increases. This improves the linear acceleration feel and the feel of increasing vehicle speed in response to the driver's accelerator operation.

Neutral control reduces engine load and improves fuel economy while the vehicle is stopped (in the D position) by disconnecting the engine from the transmission (partially releasing the starting clutch inside the automatic transmission using linear solenoid SLS). In addition, the gradient is detected by the G sensor, and neutral control is not performed on gradients above a certain level.
When driving on winding roads with ups and downs, uphill/downhill shift control restricts upshifting when it determines that the vehicle is going uphill, achieving smooth driving.

In addition, when driving downhill, if a downhill is determined from the throttle opening and vehicle acceleration and brake operation is detected, the transmission downshifts to generate an appropriate engine braking force. The system consists of the throttle position sensor and vehicle speed sensor.

Slope determination is made by comparing the reference acceleration stored in the computer with the actual acceleration calculated from the speed sensor signal. When the actual acceleration is less than the reference acceleration, an uphill road is determined, and when the actual acceleration is greater than the reference acceleration, a downhill road is determined.

Shift control sets the target input shaft speed based on information such as accelerator opening, vehicle speed and brake signal so that the optimum gear ratio and shift speed are obtained. Furthermore, a signal is output to the shift control duty solenoid (DS1,DS2) so that the speed obtained from the primary pulley speed sensor matches the target input shaft speed, optimizing the gear ratio.
In the D position, control is performed through integrated engine control to maximize fuel economy and driving performance.

In the M position of sport sequential Shiftmatic mode, M1 to M7 indicate the respective gears as shown in the illustration below. When the set vehicle speed is reached during acceleration, the transmission automatically upshifts.
Lock-up operation is performed based on a determination from the throttle opening and vehicle speed.

The lock-up operating range has been expanded compared to conventional A/T models, enabling lock-up from the low speed range. In addition, by expanding the lock-up operating range down to the low speed range during deceleration as well, the fuel cut range has been expanded, achieving excellent fuel economy.

If a malfunction is detected in the speed sensors, solenoids, etc., the check engine warning light in the combination meter assembly illuminates to warn the driver. A new diagnosis system has been adopted for serviceability. By connecting TaSCAN to DLC3, diagnosis results for malfunctioning areas can be displayed. For the list of diagnosis items, refer to the Repair Manual.
This function prevents a significant loss of drivability even if a malfunction occurs in the sensors or solenoids. For details, refer to the Repair Manual.

ITEM.PTXT: Its compact size and high transmission efficiency achieve excellent starting and acceleration performance and low fuel consumption.
A damper construction that allows lock-up operation from the low speed range has been adopted, absorbing engine torque fluctuations and achieving an excellent ride.
A compact torus shape has been adopted, making the torque converter more compact.
High rigidity is ensured by optimum placement of ribs and case shapes using FEM analysis, suppressing deformation due to loads from the gear train.
An aluminum alloy case and cover have been adopted to reduce weight.
The shape and rib arrangement have been designed to reduce vibration in the range where gear noise occurs, while minimizing any weight increase.
The torque converter and oil pump are located on the input shaft, and a planetary gear is used as the forward/reverse switching mechanism.

It consists of a continuously variable transmission mechanism made up of 1 pair of pulleys and a metal belt, a reduction gear pair, a final gear pair and a differential mechanism. Shifting is performed steplessly by varying the winding diameter of the metal belt on the pulleys, whose groove width is varied by hydraulic pressure.

ITEM.PTXT: Whereas a conventional automatic transaxle performs stepped shifting using planetary gears, the Super CVT-i automatic transaxle shifts using 1 pair of pulleys, whose groove width can be freely varied by hydraulic pressure, and a metal belt. During shifting, the pulley width is varied to shift steplessly. Furthermore, a wide gear ratio range ensures excellent fuel economy and quietness.
It consists of pulleys with pistons and a metal belt, and shifting is performed by varying the pulley width through operation of the pistons in the primary and secondary pulleys.

A double piston construction has been adopted for the primary pulley, pressing the belt with the pressure generated in two hydraulic chambers in series. This allows the outer diameter of the hydraulic chambers to be reduced, making the system more compact.
The metal belt consists of metal elements and 2 rows of steel rings.
Whereas ordinary chains and rubber belts transmit power by tension, the metal belt transmits power by the compression of the elements (pushing of the elements).
A single pinion type planetary gear has been adopted as the forward/reverse switching mechanism.
It consists of a reverse brake that holds the planetary carrier and a forward clutch that transmits engine driving force to the planetary sun gear.
A centrifugal hydraulic pressure cancel chamber is provided in the forward clutch to eliminate the centrifugal hydraulic pressure of the fluid generated by rotation, improving hydraulic response.

When moving forward, the forward clutch is engaged, and the driving force from the engine is input from the input shaft to the sun gear and output directly to the continuously variable transmission mechanism.

When reversing, the driving force from the engine is input to the ring gear. It is then input to the sun gear through the pinion gears, whose revolution is stopped by the reverse brake, and the driving force from the engine is output to the continuously variable transmission mechanism in the reverse direction of rotation.

Compared with a conventional stepped A/T, driving close to the optimum fuel economy line (a preset high-torque range with good fuel consumption rate) is possible, drawing out the maximum engine performance. In addition, by expanding the lock-up range to the low speed side, the high-efficiency range can be used during acceleration and the fuel cut range can be expanded during deceleration, contributing to low fuel consumption. The wide gear ratio range lowers engine speed during high-speed driving by making use of the high gear, achieving excellent fuel economy.
A characteristic of the CVT is that it can maintain the engine speed in the high-output range.

Unlike a conventional stepped A/T, a stepless CVT can accelerate while maintaining an efficient engine speed, so the maximum output range can be used efficiently and the driving force of the engine can be fully utilized.

In a conventional stepped A/T, the driving force characteristics of the engine (relationship between engine speed, torque and vehicle speed, etc.) are determined by each gear. Therefore, while the driving force characteristics lie on the curves drawn by each gear, with a CVT the driving force characteristics can be set freely. As a result, compared with the stepped driving force characteristics that occur with stepped shifting, smooth shift characteristics are achieved and engine characteristics can be fully utilized.

During vehicle acceleration, engine performance is fully utilized by shortening the initial time lag that occurs when the accelerator is depressed and by optimally controlling the driving force (engine speed x output shaft torque).
A non-crescent type high-pressure oil pump has been adopted, reducing the theoretical discharge volume and drive torque.

The rigidity of the valve body has been increased to handle the higher pressure of the hydraulic circuit. In addition, all solenoid valves are mounted on the lower valve body side for easier servicing.

ITEM.PTXT: In the CVT belt mechanism, the CVT belt clamping force for transmitting torque is controlled by controlling the secondary pulley hydraulic pressure. In addition, by placing a pressure control valve and solenoid valve downstream of the line pressure, the belt clamping force can be controlled with the optimum hydraulic pressure, achieving excellent power transmission performance.

Electronic control of this process increases the freedom of shift control, achieving driving that responds to the driver's intentions, as well as gear ratios and shift speeds that allow driving on the engine's optimum fuel economy line. In addition, by separating upshift and downshift control, fine control is achieved.
Reduction gears are provided as a reduction mechanism and for transmitting the driving force output from the continuously variable transmission mechanism to the differential drive pinion.
The reduction drive gear is supported by 2 independent bearings, optimizing tooth contact with the driven gear. This achieves excellent quietness.
The front differential is a 2-pinion type using helical gears for the reduction mechanism and straight bevel gears for the differential mechanism.
A parking lock gear is located at the secondary pulley. The parking lock pawl engages with the parking lock gear to lock the rotation of the transmission.

PARA.TITLE: Pulley Speed Sensors and Turbine Speed Sensor

ITEM.PTXT: The primary pulley speed sensor (NIN), which detects the input shaft speed, is located at the primary pulley, and the secondary pulley speed sensor (NOUT), which detects the output shaft speed, is located on the secondary pulley shaft (reduction drive gear).
The turbine speed sensor (NT) for lock-up engagement pressure control and forward/reverse clutch pressure control is located at the forward clutch drum.
The hydraulic pressure sensor detects the belt clamping force so that the belt clamping force can be optimally controlled.

A fluid temperature sensor is provided to perform shift control according to the fluid temperature, as well as lock-up engagement pressure control, forward/reverse clutch pressure control and belt clamping force control.

A non-contact type throttle position sensor has been adopted, using a Hall element that can extract the magnetic field strength as an electrical signal using the Hall effect, which provides an output voltage linear to the throttle valve opening angle. When the throttle valve opening angle changes, the angle of the magnetic field relative to the flow of the applied current in the Hall element changes, so the strength of the magnetic field perpendicular to the applied current changes. As a result, the change in voltage generated perpendicular to both the applied current and the magnetic field is sent to the engine control computer as the throttle valve opening angle signal. In addition, reliability is ensured by adopting a 2-system (main and sub) sensor with different output characteristics.

This is a phenomenon in which, when a current flows through a rod- or plate-shaped conductor or semiconductor and a magnetic field is applied perpendicular to it, a potential difference is generated in the direction perpendicular to both the current and the magnetic field.
This is an electronic component that uses the electromotive force generated by the potential difference in a magnetic field.
The throttle position sensor detects the opening angle with 2 systems: a main circuit and a sub circuit. If a malfunction occurs in the signal, the engine control computer switches to limp mode.

ENTRY.PTXT: If a malfunction occurs in either or both circuits, the engine control computer detects the malfunction from the voltage difference between the main circuit and sub circuit. At this time, power to the throttle motor is cut and the throttle valve is returned to a predetermined opening angle by the return spring. Limp mode driving is made possible by controlling engine output using fuel injection control and ignition timing control. Also, even if the engine control computer detects another malfunction such as in the throttle motor, limp mode driving is made possible by performing the above control.
